Where distributedComputing() Runs Tasks

Source: R/remoteComputing.R
localNode.Rd

localNode() is the local machine, sshNodes() are machines reached by ssh and slurmCluster() is a SLURM cluster reached through a login node. distributedComputing() takes one of them as on.

Usage

localNode(cores = NULL)

sshNodes(nodes = names(cores), cores = NULL)

slurmCluster(
  login,
  cores,
  array = NULL,
  walltime = NULL,
  memPerCore = 2,
  partition = NULL,
  account = NULL,
  maxRunning = NULL,
  sbatch = NULL,
  jobscript = NULL
)

Arguments

cores

The cores of every task. For sshNodes() one number for all nodes or a vector named by node. NULL (default) uses the free cores of each node, see detectFreeCores(); a node gets at most the free cores it has. For slurmCluster() the cores of each array task.

nodes

Character, the nodes, each once: ssh destinations such as "host" or "user@host" with key authentication, or "localhost" for the local machine. Defaults to the names of cores.

login

Character, the login node, an ssh destination.

array

The number of array tasks, at most one per task. NULL (default) is one per task.

walltime

The maximum runtime of an array task, "HH:MM:SS", filled into the job script. Default NULL, none: a directive or comment line of the template with a field that has no value is left out.

memPerCore

Memory per core in GB, filled into the job script. Default 2.

partition, account

Character, the partition and the account of the job. Default NULL, those of the job script.

maxRunning

The most array tasks running at once. Default NULL, no limit.

sbatch

Character vector of further options of sbatch, such as "--constraint=ib".

jobscript

Path to a job script template, in place of the one slurmTemplate() set up for login. Default NULL.

Value

An object of class dMod2Nodes or dMod2Slurm.

Details

The tasks of a job run on workers: a node is one worker, and a SLURM job has array workers, the array tasks of the job. The tasks are dealt to the workers in turn, and a worker runs the tasks dealt to it one after the other, each with cores cores. Without SLURM the processes run detached and survive the R session. With SLURM the array job is submitted on the login node through the job script template slurmTemplate() set up for it; partition, account, maxRunning and sbatch are options of sbatch, which take precedence over the #SBATCH lines of the template.

See also

distributedComputing(), slurmTemplate()

Examples

localNode(cores = 4)
#> localhost (4 cores)
sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"), cores = 10)
#> server1 (10 cores), server2 (10 cores)
sshNodes(cores = c(server1 = 24, server2 = 20))
#> server1 (24 cores), server2 (20 cores)
slurmCluster("mycluster", cores = 8, array = 32, walltime = "12:00:00")
#> SLURM cluster mycluster: 32 array tasks of 8 cores for 12:00:00
